facore:craftinginfo-decipheringstation-t:
Deciphering armor schematics
Old knowledge yields to patience.

The Deciphering Table turns blank parchment into a random armor schematic.

Preparing an attempt
Place one blank parchment on the writing surface, one Dusty armor scroll on the lectern, and a fired bowl containing at least 0.2 L of black dye or grey dye in the bowl recess. Hold ink and quill in your main hand, then hold right-click on the writing surface for three seconds.

Insight and further attempts
Every attempt consumes 0.2 L of dye. Your Insight shows how close you are to deciphering the schematic. A failed attempt preserves the parchment and Dusty armor scroll, improves your Insight, and requires five in-game hours before you can try again. The fifth attempt is guaranteed to succeed.

Success consumes the Dusty armor scroll and replaces the blank parchment with a randomly selected armor schematic.
facore:craftinginfo-hemmingstation-text:
Hemming armor
A fine edge can change the character of an entire suit.

The Hemming Crane is used to finish armor with metal rims and rivets. Hang an armor piece on the frame and place your chosen rims and rivets in the bowl. The crane will show them on the armor before they are permanently attached. Flowing particles around the armor show that you are looking at a preview rather than a finished trim.

Soldering
Only silver solder can be used. Place at least 100 units in a crucible and heat it to at least 961°C, then set the hot crucible on the crane. Hold a soldering iron against the preview to attach the rims and rivets permanently. It can be stowed neatly in the holder built into the station.

If you later want a different finish, return the armor to the crane and use tongs to remove the old trim.

Every armor collection has its own available finishes. Search the handbook for Chronicles to see what each suit can use.
facore:craftinginfo-decorationstation-te:
Decorating armor
Protection need not be plain.

The Decoration Station gives each armor piece its own work area. Place the helmet, body armor, or leg armor on the matching frame, then add the appropriate decoration and, when desired, a filled Decoration Kit to the nearby material area.

Available decorations
For helmets:
- Communis Crista
- Communis Cauda
- Communis Pennae
- Communis Pluma
- Communis Pinna
- Communis Transversa
- Regalis Crista
- Metallicus Laurea (plain only)
- Wolf helmet decoration

For body armor:
- Insignia
- Mantellum
- Wolf body decoration

For leg armor:
- Lacinia
- Wolf leg decoration

Working with bear armor
A matching bear helmet, chestplate, or leg armor can be placed in its decoration area. Its fur supplies both the bear decoration and its color, so no Decoration Kit is needed. Once its decoration has been baked into the armor, removing that bear decoration with a saw returns the original bear armor, but the rough extraction leaves it at only 5% durability.

Working with cloth
Some armor is colored directly with cloth instead of using the decorations above. Each color pile requires three identical pieces of cloth. Prepare all three piles before finishing the work; each pile controls one of the armor's three color areas. The three piles may use the same color or different colors, provided that the armor permits them.

Your choices first appear as a preview. Flowing particles around the armor show that the displayed decoration or cloth colors have not yet been permanently applied. When you are happy with the result, use the finishing tool shown by the station guide. A finished decoration can be removed later with a saw, allowing the armor to be redesigned.

Choose your decoration wisely. Removing an ordinary finished decoration is too delicate a process to recover usable material, so the removed decoration is lost.

Decoration shapes and colors vary between armor collections. Search the handbook for Chronicles to see the choices available to each suit.

Decoration colors
Communis and Regalis ornaments allow every decoration color except none. Metallicus Laurea is available only in plain. Bear and wolf decorations use black, brown, or white.

Crafting wolf decorations
A helmet decoration uses three medium pelts; a body decoration uses three large pelts; leg decorations use two large pelts. Each recipe also requires a knife. Use three charcoal for black, a full 10 L bucket of strong tannin for brown, or three chalk stones for white. The brown recipe retains the empty bucket.
facore:craftinginfo-coverstation-text:
Metallizing armor
Turn a metal plate into a new surface for old armor.

The Metallizing Cauldron prepares coating solution, applies it to armor, and removes an existing coating.

EXPECT CHEMICAL BURNS WHEN VIOLATING OSHA BY MEDDLING WITH ACID BARE-HANDED. OFFHAND TONGS RECOMMENDED.

Preparing a coating solution — 2 in-game hours
Open the lid and fill the cauldron with 10L of sulfuric acid. Immerse one metal plate and leave it to dissolve for 2 in-game hours. The acid becomes a coating solution made from that metal. A very neat four-place plate holder is built into the station, giving spare plates an equally neat place to wait for their turn.

Applying a coating — 2 in-game hours
Immerse an uncoated armor piece in the prepared metal solution and close the lid. Put five pieces of coal or charcoal into the fuel tray, close its door, and light the fuel. The coating finishes after 2 in-game hours. Applying a cover removes any existing decorations and colors from that armor piece.

Removing a coating — 2 in-game hours
Fill the cauldron with 10L of sulfuric acid and immerse coated armor. No fuel is needed. After 2 in-game hours, the coating is removed and the acid becomes that metal's coating solution. Removing a cover also removes any existing decorations and colors from the armor piece. (It's acid—what did you expect?)

Interrupting an acid reaction
While the cauldron is not burning, you may remove a dissolving plate or armor piece to cancel and reset its reaction. The liquid remains in the cauldron. This retrieval causes chemical exposure unless tongs are in your offhand.

Available coating metals vary between armor collections. Search the handbook for Chronicles to see the choices available to each suit.
